\section{Introduction}
% Your proposal text (your own words) -- keep and tighten:
Modern adversaries increasingly avoid custom malware and instead ``live off
the land,'' repurposing legitimate operating-system utilities to conduct
reconnaissance, privilege escalation, and lateral movement. Because these
binaries are trusted and ubiquitous, allow-listing and signature matching
are ineffective, and the same tools are used constantly by legitimate
administrators, producing high false-positive rates for naive anomaly
detectors~\cite{barrsmith2021survivalism,ongun2021lotl}. The research gap is
a detection approach that reasons over the \emph{behavioral context} in
which a trusted binary executes rather than the binary or command in
isolation.

\WRITE{Research question (one sentence), e.g. whether parent--child execution context separates malicious from benign use of the \emph{same} trusted binaries better than binary names. Then 3 objectives: (O1) a platform-neutral provenance-graph representation for Linux and Windows; (O2) an interpretable behavioural indicator set mapped to ATT\&CK; (O3) an evaluation against a name-based baseline using hard negatives. One sentence on significance (alert fatigue~\cite{hassan2019nodoze}). One sentence on what this progress report adds since the proposal (working implementation, two datasets, first results). Last: one sentence listing the section order (II literature, III implementation, IV results, V conclusion and plan).}

\section{Literature Review}

\subsection{Scope}
\WRITE{2 sentences: you review (i) detectors aimed at LotL / LOLBin abuse and command lines, and (ii) system-level provenance graphs for host intrusion detection; host-IDS surveys~\cite{bridges2019host,liu2019syscall,liao2013ids,buczak2016survey} give the broader context.}

\subsection{LotL and Command-Line Detection}
\WRITE{Barr-Smith et al.~\cite{barrsmith2021survivalism}: large measurement study showing how widespread LotL use is in Windows malware. Hendler et al.~\cite{hendler2018powershell}: deep neural networks on PowerShell command text. Ongun et al.~\cite{ongun2021lotl}: active learning over command lines, needs analyst labels. Outrata et al.~\cite{outrata2024obfuscation}: small language models to spot obfuscated command lines. Common limitation in your words: they judge a command \emph{by itself}, not who launched it or what it led to.}

\subsection{Provenance-Graph Detection}
\WRITE{King and Chen~\cite{king2003backtracking} started causal backtracking. SLEUTH~\cite{hossain2017sleuth}, HOLMES~\cite{milajerdi2019holmes}, POIROT~\cite{milajerdi2019poirot}: attack reconstruction and hunting from audit data with tags/rules. UNICORN~\cite{han2020unicorn}, StreamSpot~\cite{manzoor2016streamspot}, ProvDetector~\cite{wang2020provdetector}, Log2vec~\cite{liu2019log2vec}: learning on whole-system graphs. CONAN~\cite{xiong2022conan}: real-time APT detection with a state-based model. NoDoze~\cite{hassan2019nodoze} and RapSheet~\cite{hassan2020rapsheet}: triage to reduce false alarms; HERCULE~\cite{pei2016hercule} and PrioTracker~\cite{liu2018priotracker}: attack-story reconstruction and causality analysis. Surveys~\cite{zipperle2023survey,li2021survey}.}

\subsection{Critical Evaluation and Gap}
\WRITE{Your judgement, 4--5 sentences: command-only methods over-fire on admins; whole-system provenance systems are powerful but heavyweight, need large training data and kernel-level collection, and are rarely evaluated on \emph{benign use of the same LOLBins}; ML for IDS has known evaluation pitfalls~\cite{sommer2010outside}. Gap: a lightweight, interpretable, cross-platform provenance score targeted at LotL, evaluated with hard negatives. End with one-sentence review conclusion.}

\section{Research Implementation}

\subsection{Approach and Methodology}
\WRITE{Explain the hypothesis and the 4-stage pipeline in your words: (1) capture process-creation telemetry; (2) build a provenance graph per activity; (3) compute behavioural indicators; (4) score = number of indicators fired (Eq.~\ref{eq:score}); compare with a name-based baseline. Stress that indicators were defined from ATT\&CK technique descriptions, not learned.}

\begin{equation}
S(G) \;=\; \sum_{k=1}^{K} \mathbb{1}\left[\,\phi_k(G)\,\right], \qquad \hat{y}(G) = \mathbb{1}\left[\,S(G) \ge \tau\,\right]
\label{eq:score}
\end{equation}
where $G$ is the provenance graph of one activity, $\phi_k$ is the $k$-th
behavioural indicator (Table~\ref{tab:indicators}), and $\tau$ is the decision
threshold. The baseline flags $G$ if any node's image name is in a list of
well-known LotL binaries.

\subsection{System and Workflow Design}
\WRITE{Linux: UTM VM, Ubuntu Server 26.04 ARM64, auditd rule \texttt{-a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S execve,execveat -k lotl\_exec}; a harness runs each labelled activity and saves its records. Graph construction: each successful execve is a node; same-PID re-exec = \emph{exec} edge (e.g.\ bash becoming sh); child linked to parent's latest execution = \emph{fork} edge; failed execve (PATH search) dropped; keep only the task's subtree so the harness is excluded. Windows: Sysmon Event ID 1 from OTRF~\cite{otrf2020datasets}; ProcessGuid/ParentProcessGuid give edges; unit = a process whose parent started before the capture + its descendants, with the parent kept as a context node (so services.exe does not merge unrelated activity). Refer to Figs.~\ref{fig:linux} and~\ref{fig:windows}.}

\begin{table*}[!t]
\caption{Behavioural indicators $\phi_k$ and their platform-specific signals}
\label{tab:indicators}
\centering\footnotesize
\begin{tabular}{p{3.0cm}p{1.9cm}p{5.2cm}p{5.6cm}}
\toprule
\textbf{Concept} & \textbf{ATT\&CK} & \textbf{Linux (auditd) signal} & \textbf{Windows (Sysmon) signal}\\
\midrule
Decoded content to shell & T1140, T1027 & decoder (base64 -d, xxd -r, openssl -d, rev) sibling of a stdin shell & \texttt{-enc}/encoded token in a command line\\
Obfuscated command & T1027 & escape sequences, long hex/base64 tokens & script schemes (\texttt{javascript:}, \texttt{vbscript:}, \texttt{script:})\\
Remote / downloaded payload & T1105 & downloaded file later executed & URL or \texttt{/i:http} in a command line\\
Proxy / interpreter execution & T1218, T1059.006 & interpreter (python3, perl) spawns a shell & signed proxy LOLBin (mshta, regsvr32, cmstp, \dots); LOLBin spawns a child\\
Unusual execution context & T1047, T1548.002 & shell reading from a pipe & shell/admin tool with parent dllhost, WmiPrvSE, mshta, \dots\\
Execution from writable/hidden path & T1564.001, T1204 & image or script under /tmp, /dev/shm; hidden path; exec bit set there & image or payload under ProgramData, AppData, Temp\\
Persistence & T1053, T1546.004 & crontab install, shell-rc edit, systemctl enable & \texttt{schtasks /create}, Run key, \texttt{sc create}\\
Defense evasion & T1070.003, T1036.005, T1055 & history clearing; kernel-thread-like names & \texttt{mavinject /INJECTRUNNING}\\
Account manipulation & T1136 & -- & \texttt{net user /add}, admin group add\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table*}

\subsection{Tools and Technologies}
\WRITE{One short paragraph: auditd/ausearch; Sysmon via OTRF; Python with networkx (graphs), pandas, scikit-learn (metrics), matplotlib; Google Colab notebook; GitHub repository (give the URL: github.com/os01752/lotl-provenance-detection); attack emulation modelled on Atomic Red Team~\cite{atomicredteam} and GTFOBins~\cite{gtfobins}, all payloads harmless (id, whoami, uname).}

\subsection{Challenges Encountered}
\WRITE{Use your real experience (this section is easy to write honestly): (1) external SSD capped at USB~2.0 ($\approx$38~MB/s), VM moved to internal disk; (2) eBPF tooling (Tracee) not practical on the ARM64 7.0 kernel, auditd chosen; (3) auditd hex-encodes arguments with spaces, and failed PATH lookups and exec-replacement initially corrupted the graphs; (4) an early baseline counted the launching shell itself, which inflated its false positives -- fixed, and hard negatives added so the comparison is fair; (5) Splunk Attack Data auditd logs keep only command lines (no PIDs), so they cannot form graphs; OTRF chosen instead.}

\section{Experimental Results}

\subsection{Experiment Setup}
\input{dataset_table.tex}
\WRITE{Describe the two datasets using Table~\ref{tab:datasets}. Linux: benign admin tasks, including hard negatives that use the same binaries as attacks (crontab -l, chmod 755 on a script, curl download, base64 encode/decode to file, python, nested shells); emulated techniques mapped to ATT\&CK. Windows pilot: 13 OTRF datasets~\cite{otrf2020datasets}; label rule (unit contains the documented technique), payload side-effect units excluded. State clearly: Windows indicator vocabulary written after inspecting these files, so it is a feasibility pilot; the final paper freezes it and tests on unseen OTRF datasets.}

\subsection{Performance Metrics}
With $TP, FP, FN, TN$ counted per activity (Linux) or execution unit (Windows):
\begin{equation}
P=\tfrac{TP}{TP+FP},\quad R=\tfrac{TP}{TP+FN},\quad F_1=\tfrac{2PR}{P+R},\quad \mathit{FPR}=\tfrac{FP}{FP+TN}.
\end{equation}
Because the threshold $\tau$ is not learned, we report $\tau\in\{1,2\}$ and the
threshold-free ROC-AUC of $S(G)$.
